name: Ikoma Chiaki
concept: Chiaki's shoulders sit high and forward even when she stands still, as though bracing against a weight that never shifts.

answers.giri: Chiaki serves her lord Ikoma Motonobu, who has placed her under Akodo Tsukune, commander of the garrison; her duty is to report suspected traitors among the soldiers she quarters with, which means she must build their trust first.
answers.ninjo: Chiaki wants to protect the garrison from false accusation as fiercely as she investigates real treason, and each soldier she clears gnaws at her certainty that she is not simply freeing the guilty.
answers.standout_quality: Chiaki remembers every name in the garrison and every debt she owes them, which makes suspecting them of treason a discipline that costs her more than the interrogations do.
answers.accomplishment: Ikoma Chiaki turned a suspected spy's confession during interrogation into evidence that exonerated him instead, and Akodo Tsukune believed her report that the man was loyal despite her having built the case against him first.
answers.challenge: After a day spent carrying intelligence reports between the garrison's wings, Chiaki's shoulders lock and her hands move like rust, making the careful notation that keeps her soldiers' names perfect a labor that eats into the hours when she should be sleeping.
answers.peace: Chiaki spreads oracle bones across the garrison's ledger at night, reading the cracks for the names of the loyal, and each night the bones refuse to name the guilty ones clearly enough that she can stop looking.
answers.fear: Chiaki spreads the rosters across her desk each morning and sees only the names she might have to betray, which means she has stopped eating with the garrison and begun timing her patrols to walk alone.
answers.accoutrement: Chiaki keeps a tally of names scratched into the spine of her ledger, each mark a soldier she has cleared, and on the nights when no new marks come she scrapes at the old ones until her fingernail breaks.

clan_relationship.text: Chiaki keeps the garrison's rosters in her own hand and corrects the Ikoma scribes when they miswrite a name, which makes her meticulous about record-keeping in ways that serve Tsukune's investigation and undermine the clan's need for her to move unseen.

mentor.name: Kuni Eichi
mentor.text: Kuni Eichi taught Chiaki that the guilty confess to end the silence and the innocent confess to end the doubt, and that the whole craft is telling which; she has cleared eleven men since and is not sure of one of them.

answers.first_impression: Chiaki's shoulders sit high and forward even when she stands still, as though bracing against a weight that never shifts.
answers.stress_reaction: Chiaki stops answering questions during interrogations, sitting across from the suspect in complete silence until they speak again, which means the guilty confess to fill the quiet and the innocent begin to doubt whether she believes them at all.
answers.relationships:
Toritaka Emiko (Falcon) — Toritaka Emiko shelters Chiaki in her quarters when the interrogations leave her unable to eat in the garrison mess, and Chiaki has begun to wonder whether Emiko knows the garrison better than its own commander does.
Kitsu Kinuko (Lion) — Kitsu Kinuko comes to the garrison library where Chiaki keeps the rosters and sits with her in the dark before dawn, reading the same ledger page twice without speaking, and Chiaki has never asked her why but knows it means Kinuko does not believe the names written there either.

parent_opinion.description: Ikoma Chiaki's mother has stopped asking when she will come home for the festival, knowing now that her daughter will spend the evening alone with the garrison rosters instead of with her family.

answers.death: Chiaki expects to die in the library, alone with the rosters, when her heart simply stops and no one finds her until morning.

Ikoma Chiaki's garrison commander Akodo Tsukune taught her to read silence for the tremor that betrays guilt, but Chiaki has learned that the soldiers who go quiet around her are often the ones with nothing left to hide.

Chiaki's mother taught her to keep the garrison's rosters by hand, in her own handwriting, so that no scribe could slip a name through unnoticed; now the meticulous work that was meant to protect her soldiers binds her to each one so tightly that suspecting them feels like suspecting the hand that holds the pen.
